According to data from Counterpoint Research, although global smartphone shipments have declined overall, Apple still captured nearly half of global smartphone revenue in the second quarter. Details are as follows.

Apple achieved its highest-ever revenue share record in the second quarter

A new report from Counterpoint Research (cited via MacMagazine) indicates that Apple's share of global smartphone revenue reached a historic high of 49% last quarter, with revenue growing 22% year-on-year, marking the highest revenue share the company has ever recorded in a second quarter.

Counterpoint noted that global smartphone revenue grew 7% year-on-year during the quarter, and Apple posted the fastest growth among the top five brands. Its average selling price rose from US$879 a year ago to US$946.

Apple's shipment share in the second quarter also hit an all-time high, climbing from 17% a year ago to 21%. However, Apple still ranks second behind Samsung, whose global shipment share stands at 23%. Among the remaining top five brands, shipment shares all declined, with Xiaomi seeing the largest drop, falling from 14% to 11%, representing a 26% year-on-year decrease in shipments.

Counterpoint pointed out that the entire industry is facing a memory shortage, forcing several smartphone manufacturers to raise prices due to rising component costs and tight supply. Apple has largely maintained stable iPhone pricing, though Counterpoint expects this situation to change in the coming quarters.
